CLXIV. Ego Benessius cum fratre meo germano Przibikone de Krzemze ac alio Przybikone fratre nostro de Chlvm omnes vnanimiter et vna voce constare desideramus vniuersis presencium noticiam habituris, quod bona deliberacione maturoque consilio prehabitis omnes cou- corditer de bonis nostris hereditariis in villa Kamcnn habitis in hereditatibus, quas Peter Griss Hoffuel Jacob Czugwaich et Eblinus incole ville illius possidere dinoscuntur, vendidimus iusto titulo ven- dicionis nobili domino nostro domino Johanni de Rosennberk duas sexageuas redituum cum quatuor grossis grossorum Pragensium annui et perpetui census cum omnibus juribus vtilitatibus obvencio- nibiis bernis robotis exaccionibus bonoranciis causis judicialibus emendis deuolucionibus et generaliter omnibus prouentibus, quibus- cunque nominibus censeantur, ac omni pleno dominio, prout nos ipsi tenuimus nichil penitus nobis jurisdictionis aut proprietatis ibidem reseruantes, sed < nme jus, quod ibidem habuimus, in ipsum dominum Jobannem et eum, qui presentem litteram de sua voluntate habuerit, omnimode transfundentes, pro triginta vna sexagenis grossorum Pra gensium, quas illico ab eo percepimus, cum paratis pecuniis integra- liter persolutas. Promittimus igitur sincera fide nostra sine dolo omnes manu coniuncta et indiuisa eandem hereditatem cum suo censu preexpresso a quolibet impetente, cuiuscunque status fuerit aut �?o idicionis, jure ter re nostre Bohem ¡e funditus et plenarie liber 193 tare et disbrigare et singulariter a dotaliciis mulierum, si qua in illa hereditate emergerent impedimenta. Et quia nos prefati Benessius et Przibiko de Kremz hereditatem pretactam ad manus nostras tene- mus tabulis regni nobis roboratam, ideo ne per heredes aut succes- sores nostros aliqualis in postermn questio suboriatur, promittimus specialiter pro nobis heredibus et successoribus nostris vniuersis, eandem vendicionem firmam et inconwlsam perpetuis temporibus ob- seruare. Si vero qualiscunque in eo instancia oriretur et eandem hereditatem nos omnes prenominati Benesius et Przibiko de Kremz et Przibiko de Chlum secundum jura terre non exbrigaremus, tune in aliis nostris propriis liberis et eque valentibus hereditatibus de toti- dem censibus et cum augmento tercie partis condescendere promit timus et debemus omnibus occasionibus penitus postergatis. Quod si non faceremus, tune duo nostrum, qui primo mouiti fuerimus, vnus alterius per absenciam aut incurabilitatem se penitus excusare non valentes ciuitatem Chrumpnaw intrare debemus, quilibet cum vno famulo et duobus equis ad obstagiandum in hospicio nobis per domi- num Johannem aut presencium habitorem deputato, nee exire aliquo jure, quousque omnia prescripta. ad effectum finaliter perducamus. Elapsis autem quatuordecim diehus continuis a monicione nobis de obstagio facta prestito per nos obstagio vol non prestito sepetactus dominus Johannes aut possessor presencium pecuniam prefatam tri- ginta vnius sexagenarum cuín augmento tercie partis recipiendi inter Judeos seu Christianos nostrum omnium super dampna plenum obti- nent potestutem. Nos quoque continue obstagiare sumus astricti, donec de pecuniis preexpressis eciam cum augmento tercie partis ac vniuersis dampnis occasione non solucionis et nostre incurabilitatis quocunque modo contractis, per nos plene et omuimode fuerit satis- factum. Insuper quicunque banc litteram de domini Johannis bona habuerit voluntate, eidem jus competit omnium premissorum. In quorum omnium euidentiam et roboramentum sigilla nostra propria de certa nostra scientia presentibus sunt appensa. entries.english:
1385, 21 March. Benesch and Pfibiko von Krems and Pfibiko von Chlum sell to Lord Hans von Rosenberg an annual rent of two score and four Prague groschen in the village of Kamen for 31 score Prague groschen.

CLXIV. I, Benessius, with my full brother Przibiko de Krems and our other brother Przybiko de Chlum, jointly and unanimously make known to all who see this document that, after careful deliberation and mature counsel, we have sold by lawful sale, from our hereditary properties in the village of Kamen, where Peter Griss, Hoffuel, Jacob Czugwaich, and Eblinus, residents of that village, hold their estates, to our noble lord Lord Hans von Rosenberg an annual and perpetual rent of two score and four Prague groschen, with all rights, benefits, revenues, taxes, labor services, levies, judicial dues, fines, reversions, and all proceeds by whatever names they are called, and full lordship, as we ourselves held it, reserving no jurisdiction or ownership there, but wholly transferring to Lord Johann and whoever holds this charter with his consent all the right we had there. The price is 31 score Prague groschen, which we have received from him at once in full, in ready money.

We jointly promise in good faith and without deceit to warrant and defend this estate and its stated rent, under the law of our Bohemian land, against every claimant of any status or condition, including any impediment arising from a woman’s dower. Since we, Benessius and Przibiko of Krems, hold the estate in our hands, confirmed to us in the land registers, and so that no dispute may later arise through our heirs or successors, we specifically promise for ourselves and all our heirs and successors to keep this sale firm and unaltered forever. If any claim arises and we fail under the law of the land to defend the estate, we promise to provide equivalent unencumbered hereditary properties yielding the same rents, increased by one third, setting aside every objection. If we fail to do this, two of us, whoever is first summoned, must enter the town of Krumlov, neither excusing himself because the other is absent or incapacitated, and remain under arrest in a lodging assigned by Lord Johann or the bearer of this charter, each with one servant and two horses, until we fulfill everything stated above. After fourteen full days from notice to enter custody, whether or not we have done so, Lord Johann or the holder of this charter may recover the stated 31 score with one-third increase from any of us, among Jews or Christians, and obtain full compensation for all losses. We must remain in custody until the sums, increase, and all losses caused by non-payment or our default are fully satisfied. Whoever holds this charter with Lord Johann’s consent has the right to all the foregoing. Our own seals are attached in witness and confirmation. In the year 1385, on the feast day of Saint Benedict the Confessor.

Three small seals hang from parchment strips, in green wax (a), and white wax (b and c); all show a helmet adorned with an arrow. The inscriptions identify Benesius and the two Przibikos.
